title: Fixed-scalar derived presentations and supplied local constant models
statement: Let C be a small category and J a Grothendieck topology on it, and let B be a commutative ring in the same universe. Constant-scalar restriction [def-pe-etale-constructible-module] from intrinsic modules over the constant B-ring to B-module-valued sheaves is an additive exact equivalence. Define its exact induced functor on the standard derived localizations, and define exact derived restriction to each actual slice J/U. A supplied local model for an intrinsic derived object K at U is an ordinary cochain complex M of B-modules together with existence of an isomorphism from the restriction of fixed-scalar K to the localization of the termwise constant sheaf of M. This is only an isomorphism predicate and chooses no model or witness. The derived categories and localizations are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Use the already proved constant-scalar equivalence; addition is pointwise, hence the equivalence is additive. Equivalences preserve finite limits and finite colimits.
Restriction to J/U is precomposition by Over.forget U, hence additive and left exact. The cocontinuous forgetful functor gives a right adjoint to this restriction, proving colimit preservation.

Use the standard localization for every intrinsic and fixed module category. Apply the exact-functor mapDerivedCategory construction to scalar restriction and slice restriction, and define the local-model predicate by the displayed isomorphism.
